audits.title: 763 QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (QIP) ON IMPROVING THE USE OF THE CLINICAL FRAILTY SCALE (CFS) DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
audits.standard: CFS documented on admission for patients over 65 with COVID-19
audits.setting: Acute hospital trust, COVID-19 admissions over 65

cycle1.result: 42% had a CFS documented during admission.

audits.intervention: PDSA cycles: trust-wide email, reminder emails and WhatsApp messages, then an e-poster screensaver on trust computers for 2 weeks.

cycle2.result: CFS compliance 68% after the second intervention.

audits.other_findings: Compliance was 65% after the first intervention; 80 patients reviewed in total, and all with CFS 5 or above had DNACPR decisions.
audits.citation: . 763 QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (QIP) ON IMPROVING THE USE OF THE CLINICAL FRAILTY SCALE (CFS) DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. Age Ageing. 2022;51(Suppl 1).

audits.title: Audit Of Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) Screening In Medical Assessment Unit (MAU) Admitted Patients In A Model-2 Hospital
audits.standard: Local frailty screening pathway: all MAU patients aged 75 or over screened with the Clinical Frailty Scale using a bespoke sticker; CFS 6 or more triggers referral to the CNS for the Older Adult
audits.setting: Medical Assessment Unit, Mallow General Hospital (Model-2 hospital), Cork

cycle1.result: Of 94 eligible patients (of 247 attendees), 81% (n=77) had a bespoke sticker and 71% of these were completed (n=55). Of 40 admitted, 57.5% (n=23) referred and seen by CNS, 35% (n=14) appropriately not referred, 2.5% (n=1) not referred but should have been, 5% (n=2) referred but not seen.

audits.other_findings: Median CFS of admitted screened patients was 6; 5% of admissions would have benefited from CNS input but did not get it.
audits.citation: Costello C, Woulfe C, Daly S, Jennings E. Audit Of Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS) Screening In Medical Assessment Unit (MAU) Admitted Patients In A Model-2 Hospital. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae178.276.

audits.title: 92 Clinical Frailty Scoring Is Crucial For the COVID-19 Era and Beyond
audits.standard: CFS documentation and treatment escalation plan at clerking, post-take and ward admission (NICE NG159); audit standard 100%
audits.setting: Six wards, Royal Free Hospital (inpatients over 65)

cycle1.result: CFS documented in 7% at clerking and post-take and 13% on ward admission.

audits.intervention: Teaching sessions, promotion of the CFS mobile app, a post-take sticker and an elderly medicine ward admission proforma.

cycle2.result: CFS documentation 17% at clerking and post-take and 24% on ward admission.

audits.other_findings: Treatment escalation plans present in 50% of patients; CFS not yet widely used in escalation decisions.
audits.citation: White L, Tyler A, Samji A. 92 Clinical Frailty Scoring Is Crucial For the COVID-19 Era and Beyond. Age Ageing. 2021;50(Suppl 1):i12-i42.

audits.title: Acute frailty services: results of a national day of care survey.
audits.standard: Use of a validated frailty assessment tool (clinical frailty scale) within 24 h of admission in patients aged 70 and over
audits.setting: 152 UK acute hospitals, Society for Acute Medicine Benchmarking Audit day of care

cycle1.result: 1626 (45.1%) patients aged 70 and over assessed with a validated frailty tool; 117 (90.0%) hospitals reported using a validated tool and 57 (42.2%) had an acute frailty unit.

audits.other_findings: Assessment by acute frailty services associated with same-day discharge (adjusted OR 1.55, 95% CI 1.03-2.39); wide variation in service design.
audits.citation: Kamwa V, Knight T, Atkin C, Cooksley T, Subbe C, Holland M, et al.. Acute frailty services: results of a national day of care survey. BMC Geriatr. 2024;24(1):608. doi:10.1186/s12877-024-05075-1. PMID: 39014306.

audits.title: Identifying frail patients at the front door: a quality improvement project on improving identifying frailty and accuracy of Clinical Frailty Scale in the emergency department in an acute general hospital.
audits.standard: NHS England CQUIN 05 (2023/24): identify frailty in ED patients aged 65+ using the Clinical Frailty Scale, CGA if CFS 6 or above. SMART target 70% correct identification of CFS 6+ by November 2024; ED nurse scores compared with frailty intervention team scores.
audits.setting: Emergency department, John Radcliffe Hospital, Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (acute general hospital)

cycle1.result: Correct identification of moderate frailty (CFS 6+) 45–51%; exact CFS accuracy 17%.

audits.intervention: Two PDSA cycles of ED nurse training: CFS lanyard card to standardise scoring, 1:1 brief teaching (135 sessions), group/virtual sessions, posters, newsletter and emails (cycle 1, November 2023); plus quizzes, scenarios and individual feedback (cycle 2, September to October 2024).

cycle2.result: Correct identification of CFS 6+ rose to 74–78% (78% at 9–13 October 2024); exact CFS accuracy up to 42%.

audits.other_findings: After cycle 1 correct identification rose to 70% then ranged 58–68%; exact accuracy rose to 30% but fell back to 17%, so sustainability of accuracy is uncertain.
audits.citation: Zhang Y, Cosimetti A, Montagu A. Identifying frail patients at the front door: a quality improvement project on improving identifying frailty and accuracy of Clinical Frailty Scale in the emergency department in an acute general hospital. BMJ Open Qual. 2025;14(2):e003216. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2024-003216. PMID: 40210247.
